input.reason: A finite input can provide zero allocation-failure limit, a main URL and well-formed XML with an xi:include carrying an invalid parse value; the entry passes that document to XInclude processing.

evidence.dependency_reason: Encoded input strings delimit the URL and XML entity.
The first supplied entity becomes the main URL and document.

lifecycle.reason: For a successfully parsed document and allocated XInclude context, the OLD entry processes the node while the context is live and then frees the context and document.

evidence.dependency_reason: Creates and initializes the context for the parsed document.
Frees the context and its owned state.

control_flow.reason: The entry calls xmlXIncludeProcessNode on the parsed document; processing traverses to xi:include, expands it, reads its parse attribute and can raise an XInclude error. The context callback is consulted at that error site.

evidence.dependency_reason: The public operation enters root processing after its argument guards.
Traverses the document and expands recognized include nodes.
An invalid parse attribute reaches the XInclude error producer.
The error producer forwards the context callback and data.

blockers.requirement: The XInclude-context operation must be able to deliver XInclude and delegated parser or XPointer errors to a context-local structured callback with its supplied data.
blockers.target_route: The OLD entry reads a main XML entity, parses it, creates an xmlXIncludeCtxt, sets flags and calls xmlXIncludeProcessNode. A finite well-formed document containing xi:include with an invalid parse value reaches xmlXIncludeErr. The changed setter can install the structured callback on that same context, and included-document parsing and XPointer evaluation conditionally forward it.
blockers.failure_condition: The OLD entry never calls xmlXIncludeSetErrorHandler. xmlXIncludeNewContext zero-initializes errorHandler and errorCtxt, leaving the context-local structured route unreachable for every input.
blockers.alternative_paths: Input bytes only determine options and entities, not the private callback fields. The initializer installs a generic variadic error function, whose signature and registration differ from a context-local structured callback. The included-parser and XPointer forwarding paths both require the same non-NULL context callback, so they provide no equivalent route.
